nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, an arc set on $n$ points is a finite set of ordered pairs $(i, j)$, called arcs, with $i, j \in \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Arc sets

nodes.summary: The block count of an arc set $P$ on $n$ points is $n - |P|$, where the subtraction is truncated at $0$.
nodes.title: Block count

nodes.summary: An arc set $P$ on $n$ points is noncrossing when every arc $(i, j) \in P$ has $i < j$ and any two distinct arcs $(i, j)$ and $(k, l)$ of $P$ satisfy $i \ne k$, $j \ne l$, and not $i < k < j < l$. So distinct arcs do not cross and share neither a left nor a right endpoint.
nodes.title: Noncrossing arc sets

nodes.summary: The block-count homomesy claim holds: with $\sigma_n$ the toggle composite on $n$ points and $\sigma_n^k$ its $k$-fold iterate, for every $n \ge 1$, every noncrossing arc set $P$ on $n$ points and every $L \ge 1$ with $\sigma_n^L(P) = P$, twice the sum of the block counts of $P, \sigma_n(P), \dots, \sigma_n^{L-1}(P)$ equals $L(n + 1)$.
nodes.title: Block-count homomesy for toggling noncrossing partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma_n$ be the toggle composite on $n$ points and $\sigma_n^k$ its $k$-fold iterate. The claim states that for every $n \ge 1$, every noncrossing arc set $P$ on $n$ points and every $L \ge 1$ with $\sigma_n^L(P) = P$, twice the sum of the block counts of $P, \sigma_n(P), \dots, \sigma_n^{L-1}(P)$ equals $L(n + 1)$. That is, the number of blocks is homomesic under $\sigma_n$ with average $(n + 1)/2$.
nodes.title: Block-count homomesy claim for toggling noncrossing partitions

nodes.summary: The toggle composite $\sigma$ on $n$ points sends an arc set $P$ on $n$ points to the arc set obtained from $P$ by applying the toggles $\tau_{i,j}$ at the arcs $(i, j)$ of the toggle order on $n$ points one after another, in the order of that list.
nodes.title: Toggle composite

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the toggle order on $n$ points is the list of all arcs $(i, i + d)$ with $d \ge 1$, $i \ge 0$ and $i + d \le n - 1$, ordered by length $d = 1, \dots, n - 1$ and, for each length, by increasing left endpoint $i$. In $1$-indexed form it is $(1,2), (2,3), \dots, (n-1,n), (1,3), \dots, (n-2,n), \dots, (1,n)$.
nodes.title: Toggle order

nodes.summary: For an arc $a = (i, j)$ and an arc set $P$ on $n$ points, the toggle $\tau_{i,j}$ sends $P$ to $P \setminus \{a\}$ if $a \in P$; otherwise to $P \cup \{a\}$ if $P \cup \{a\}$ is a noncrossing arc set; and otherwise it leaves $P$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Toggle at an arc

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
